note.explanation: Elements, compounds and mixtures differ in what they contain and whether their particles are chemically joined. Elements contain one kind of atom; compounds contain elements chemically combined in fixed ratios; mixtures contain substances mixed without chemical bonding.
examples: Water (H₂O) is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
Salt water is a mixture: salt and water are mixed, and the salt can be separated by physical methods.
note.checkAnswer: A compound contains elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio; a mixture contains components that are not chemically bound together.
note.simple: An element has one kind of atom. A compound has different elements chemically joined. A mixture has substances together but not chemically joined.

examTips: Board questions may ask you to define an element, compound or mixture, or to compare their properties in a table.

Use textbook examples such as H₂O for a compound, salt solution for a homogeneous mixture and rock for a heterogeneous mixture.
When asked about mixture properties, mention that each component retains its identity and that the mixture's properties are the sum of those of its components.

explain.title: Elements
explain.body: An element is the simplest form of matter. It is a pure substance containing the same kind of atoms. It is not possible to break down an element into simpler particles by ordinary chemical reactions.

explain.title: Compounds
explain.body: A compound is a pure substance. It is formed by the chemical combination of two or more atoms of different elements. In a compound, the atoms of elements must combine together by a fixed ratio by weight. A compound can be broken into its constituent elements by a chemical reaction.

explain.title: Mixtures
explain.body: Mixture is an impure compound. A sample of matter having more than one type of elements or compounds mixed together in any ratio, is called a mixture. Its components are not chemically bound together, retain their identities and specific properties, and can be separated by physical methods.

explain.title: Examples and forms
explain.body: Water (H₂O) and ammonia (NH₃) are compounds. A salt solution in water is a homogeneous mixture, while a sample of rock is a heterogeneous mixture. Mixtures have the combined properties of their components.

mistakes: Do not call a mixture a compound: mixtures are not chemically bound together, while compounds are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
Do not say that components of a mixture lose their properties; each component retains its identity and specific properties.
Do not confuse homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures: salt solution is homogeneous, while a sample of rock is heterogeneous.
Do not say a compound can be separated by physical methods; breaking it into its constituent elements requires a chemical reaction.
